summary: LLM inference costs are dominated by token volume, and in 2026 the paradox is that even as per-token prices fell ~80% between 2025 and 2026, total enterprise API spend keeps doubling (past $8.4B in 2025) because usage is growing faster than prices drop. Systematic optimization—combining prompt caching, model routing, semantic caching, compression, and output control—routinely cuts production LLM bills by 50-80% with no loss in output quality. The highest-leverage lever is prompt caching (up to 90% off repeated prefixes), while model routing alone can cut per-query costs 60-80% by sending easy queries to cheaper models.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix/KV caching)
techniques.description: Caches the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, tool definitions) so the provider doesn't reprocess it on every call. Structural saving with no change to output quality. Requires ordering prompts so the static portion stays at the front and truly static.
techniques.savings: 41-90% reduction on input tokens for repeated prefixes (59-70% typical)
techniques.example: Place your 10,000-token system prompt and tool schema first, then append the user's dynamic message last; Anthropic/OpenAI then charge a fraction (e.g. ~10%) for the cached prefix on subsequent calls. Avoid putting dynamic tool results in the cached prefix, which can paradoxically raise latency.

techniques.name: Model Routing (tiered model selection)
techniques.description: Routes each query to the cheapest model that can handle it—simple/FAQ queries go to budget-tier models, only complex reasoning escalates to flagship models. Can be rule-based, classifier-based, or confidence-cascade based.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5, 25% to a mid-tier model, and only 5% of hard queries to GPT-4-class models; a $0.15/$0.60 budget model vs a $2.50/$10.00 flagship is a ~16x cost difference for identical token counts.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches answers by meaning rather than exact string match, using embedding similarity so paraphrased but equivalent queries ('how do I cancel my subscription?' vs 'cancel my plan how?') return a cached response. The second-most-adopted technique after prompt caching. Requires careful similarity-threshold tuning to avoid serving wrong answers.
techniques.savings: 30-50% cost reduction on conversational workloads (typical 45% cache hit rate)
works_with: any provider (implemented in your gateway/app layer)
techniques.example: Embed each incoming query, and if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds ~0.92, return the stored answer instead of calling the LLM—tune the threshold conservatively to prevent false-positive matches on distinct questions.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Response Caching
techniques.description: Stores full responses keyed on the exact input string (plus model/params) and returns them instantly for repeated identical requests. Cheapest and safest cache layer, best combined with semantic caching in a multi-tier strategy.
techniques.savings: 100% cost + latency elimination on exact repeats (overall impact varies with repeat rate)
techniques.example: Hash the full prompt+parameters as a Redis key with a TTL; identical FAQ or boilerplate requests return from cache in milliseconds with zero token spend.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces input tokens by removing redundancy—trimming verbose instructions, deduplicating few-shot examples, summarizing long context, and using token-efficient formats (e.g. compact JSON over verbose prose) or tools like LLMLingua.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through LLMLingua to compress a 4,000-token context to ~2,400 tokens while preserving key facts before passing it to the model.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Caps and shapes output tokens—which cost 4-5x input tokens on flagship models—via max_tokens limits, explicit 'be concise' instructions, and structured/JSON schemas that prevent rambling.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct the model to 'answer in one short paragraph, no preamble' for a classification or summarization endpoint to avoid paying for unused verbose output.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through a provider's asynchronous batch API, which processes jobs within a window (e.g. 24h) at a steep discount versus real-time calls.
techniques.example: Send overnight bulk tasks like document classification or embedding generation to the OpenAI Batch API for roughly half the standard per-token price.

techniques.name: Retrieval/Context Trimming (RAG optimization)
techniques.description: Retrieves and injects only the most relevant chunks instead of stuffing the whole knowledge base into context, cutting input tokens and often improving answer accuracy. Includes reranking and top-k tuning.
techniques.savings: 40-70% reduction in context tokens vs naive full-context stuffing
techniques.example: Instead of passing 20 retrieved chunks, rerank and keep only the top 3-5 most relevant, reducing a 6,000-token context to under 2,000 while raising answer precision.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Manages conversational history by summarizing or truncating older turns rather than resending the entire growing transcript, preventing linear token-cost growth in long chatbot sessions.
techniques.example: After every 10 turns, replace the raw history with a 200-token running summary plus the last 2 verbatim exchanges, keeping context bounded.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Observability
techniques.description: Continuously tracks token usage, cost per endpoint, cache hit rates, and model mix so regressions and expensive patterns are caught early. Not a direct saver but the foundation that makes every other lever measurable.
techniques.savings: Indirect—surfaces 10-30% of wasted spend that would otherwise go unnoticed
works_with: any provider via Helicone, Langfuse, LiteLLM, OpenAI usage dashboards
techniques.example: Add a Helicone or Langfuse proxy to log token counts and cost per feature, then alert when any endpoint's daily spend exceeds its baseline by 50%.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity; integrates with LangChain and multiple vector stores.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted; you pay only underlying infra/vector-DB costs)

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store widely used for exact-match response caching and, via RediSearch vector capabilities, semantic caching of LLM responses for low-latency reuse.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; Redis Cloud managed from ~$5/month, enterprise tiers usage-based

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source proxy/SDK giving a unified OpenAI-compatible API across 100+ models, with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, rate limiting, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise with SSO/support via custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing cost/token logging, caching, rate limiting, and prompt analytics via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k logs/mo); paid plans from ~$20/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM observability and analytics platform for tracing, token/cost tracking, evaluation, and prompt management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted and free cloud tier; cloud paid plans from ~$29/month

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, GPTCache) plus abstractions for routing, retrieval, and context management.
tools.pricing_paid: Framework free/open-source; LangSmith observability paid from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt-compression toolkit that shortens prompts and retrieved context using a small language model while preserving key information.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway routing requests across many providers/models with automatic fallbacks and price-based routing, useful for cost-driven model selection.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use; pay-as-you-go pass-through on model usage plus small fee

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering caching (simple + semantic), model routing, load balancing, observability, and guardrails through a single API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$49/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: NeuralTrust
tools.description: AI gateway and security/observability platform providing token optimization, caching, and governance for production LLM deployments.

quick_wins: Turn on provider prompt caching and reorder prompts so static system instructions, tool schemas, and few-shot examples come first—up to 90% off repeated input tokens with zero quality change.
Add model routing so simple queries hit a budget model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only hard ones escalate to a flagship—often a 16x per-query cost difference.
Cap output with max_tokens and a 'be concise, no preamble' instruction, since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens.
Drop in an exact-match response cache (Redis) for repeated/FAQ requests to eliminate 100% of token cost on identical calls.
Add a monitoring proxy (Helicone or Langfuse) to see cost per endpoint and cache hit rate before optimizing anything else, so you fix the biggest line item first.
